subject: Activation queue & schema gating for streamed toolcalls
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Activation queue & schema gating for streamed toolcalls

Hi Emily —

Great to meet you on the call earlier. As discussed, we want to make the initial enablement for streaming + function/tool-calling as low risk as possible while giving your engineers a clear path to go live. Attached is a compact activation checklist and the schema draft you shared annotated with our gating recommendations.

High level plan I propose (1–2 week initial runway):
- Week 0: confirm schema + mapping + single test endpoint
- Week 1: run 2–3 end-to-end integration tests with real traffic samples (staging)
- Week 1.5: go/no-go review and data retention alignment

Immediate asks for PulseHealth: please confirm who will own the staging API key, and share a representative sample of tool payloads (max 5) so we can pre-populate our schema validator.

I copied Monica and Soojin from CS/implementation to coordinate the mutual action plan and SOW edits.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Success, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: redwood_activation_checklist.xlsx, pulsehealth_stream_schema_v1.2.json
From: Emily Chen <emily@pulsehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: PulseHealth Implementation Team <impl-team@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Activation queue & schema gating for streamed toolcalls

Thanks Rishi —

This looks good and aligned with our internal timeline. Emily (me) will own the staging key. I attached a zip of 3 example tool payloads in my reply (referenced inline). We can also do the E2E tests on Friday morning PT — does that work for your team?

Quick notes:
- We prefer strict JSON schema validation for function outputs — our security team wants to avoid freeform objects in production.
- Retention: 90 days for staged logs, then purge unless flagged.

I'll confirm the time and upload the payloads to the Drive link you provided.

—Emily
Emily Chen
Senior PM, Integrations — PulseHealth
emily@pulsehealth.com

Attachments referenced: pulse_payloads_examples.zip

Date: 2026-05-19T02:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Activation queue & schema gating for streamed toolcalls

Thanks both — looping internal implementation. Suggested internal owners and next steps (quick):

- Soojin: lead schema validation and test harness setup (we'll add a pre-commit hook on the schema repo).
- Rishi: coordinate customer-facing checklist and confirm Friday E2E window.
- Monica: update SOW with explicit gating criteria and acceptability thresholds.

Action items I will own:
1) Draft gating criteria (pass = 3/3 E2E tests, no schema violations, latency < 300ms median) — ETA 24 hours.
2) Add minimal rollback plan to SOW (auto-fallback to non-streamed endpoints).

Soojin — can you confirm you can have the validator up by Thursday EOD PST?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Thanks Monica — I can have a lightweight validator and a test harness ready by Thursday EOD PST. Plan:
- Add a simple CLI validator that runs the 3 example payloads against pulsehealth_stream_schema_v1.2.json
- Expose a small mock endpoint in staging that returns the structured JSON + function-call metadata so the customer can exercise the full flow
- Add a GitHub Actions job to fail on schema violations (pre-commit is fine as long as we gate the main branch)

I'll push the initial validator to the shared drive link and ping the team when ready.

—Soojin

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T13:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Activation queue & schema gating for streamed toolcalls

Emily — thanks for the quick reply and for owning the key. Friday 10:00am PT works for our E2E window; I've booked a 60-minute slot and shared the calendar invite.

Summary of what we will cover during the Friday run (agenda):
1) Smoke test: key/permissions + endpoint connectivity (10m)
2) Schema validation: run 3 example payloads through Soojin's validator (15m)
3) Streamed function-call flow: observe tool invocation, structured JSON payloads, and verify observability traces (20m)
4) Go/no-go & next steps: confirm gating checklist items and sign SOW edits (15m)

Please upload the payloads to the Drive folder prior to the test and confirm the staging key by Thursday 5pm PT so we can pre-seed the harness. I'll also attach a short one-page runbook to the calendar invite.

See you Friday —
Rishi
Senior Customer Success, Redwood Inference
